_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 2.6. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: Under s. 28 CDA 1998, when must hostility be demonstrated for limb (a)?
options: At the time of committing the offence, or immediately before or after

questions.scenario: Limb (b) requires the offence to be motivated by hostility…
D attacks a Sikh man, wrongly believing him to be Muslim and shouting anti-Muslim abuse. Is it aggravated?
options: Yes – hostility based on presumed membership counts
Only if the victim is Muslim

questions.scenario: D assaults a white woman because she is married to a Black man, shouting racist abuse about him. Is it aggravated?
options: No – hostility must be to the victim's own race
Yes – membership includes association with members of a racial group

questions.scenario: In R v Rogers (2007), shouting 'bloody foreigners' at Spanish women was held to be…
options: Racial – a group defined by being non-British is a racial group

questions.scenario: Which groups have been recognised as ethnic (racial) groups?
Muslims are protected by s. 28 as a…
D assaults a taxi driver over a fare dispute but uses racist abuse during the assault. Is it aggravated?
options: No – the motive was the fare
Yes – limb (a): hostility demonstrated at the time; motive is irrelevant
Only if the driver was upset

questions.scenario: Does it matter that the hostility was also based on another factor (e.g. the victim being a traffic warden)?
options: No – it's immaterial that hostility is also based on other factors
Yes – it must be solely racial

questions.scenario: Which basic offences have racially or religiously aggravated forms under ss. 29–32?
options: Assaults (s. 20, s. 47, common), criminal damage, public order (ss. 4, 4A, 5) and harassment/stalking

questions.scenario: What is the maximum penalty for racially aggravated criminal damage (⚠)?
A robbery is motivated by hostility to the victim's sexual orientation. How is this dealt with?
options: It cannot be taken into account
Sentence uplift under s. 66 Sentencing Act 2020

questions.scenario: Which characteristics are covered by the s. 66 Sentencing Act 2020 uplift?
options: Race, religion, disability, sexual orientation, transgender identity

questions.scenario: Following DPP v Woods, must the victim actually be upset by racist words for limb (a)?
If the jury isn't sure about the racial aggravation, what can happen?
A 'religious group' includes groups defined by reference to…
options: Religious belief or lack of religious belief

questions.scenario: What is the maximum penalty for racially aggravated common assault (⚠)?
Is a racially aggravated s. 5 Public Order Act offence imprisonable (⚠)?
D sprays a racist slogan on a mosque wall when nobody is around. Which limb is most likely?
options: (b) – motivated by hostility towards members of a religious group
explanations: No victim present to demonstrate towards.
